Avocado Cream vs Glutathione Cream: Which One Suits Your Skin?

By Mohammed Nihal, founderPublished 24 October 2026Updated 16 October 20266 min read
Quick answer

Avocado cream is about moisture and comfort, so it suits dry, tight-feeling skin. Glutathione cream is radiance-focused, for a brighter, more radiant-looking finish over 8–12 weeks. Many people use both on alternate nights, with sunscreen every morning. Neither changes your natural skin colour.

  • Avocado cream: comfort and softness, often felt by the next morning.
  • Glutathione cream: a gradual, brighter-looking finish over 8–12 weeks.
  • Alternating nights makes both jars last longer.
  • Both Mirc Glow creams contain kojic acid, so wear sunscreen daily.

Avocado cream vs glutathione cream comes down to one question: what is bothering you more, dry and tight-feeling skin, or skin that looks dull and tired? Avocado cream is about comfort and softness. Glutathione cream is about a brighter, more radiant-looking finish.

Neither is "better". They do different jobs, and plenty of people end up using both. We make both, so here is an honest side-by-side, including when one of them isn't worth your money.

What avocado cream is really for

Avocado brings natural oils and a soft, buttery feel. In a night cream, that means a layer that sits on your skin while you sleep and keeps it from drying out. If your face feels tight ten minutes after washing, or you get flaky patches beside the nose in a Delhi winter, this is the cream that makes the most difference, fast.

Our Avocado Night Cream (30 g, ₹649) is the richest one we make. The Avocado Korean Night Cream (25 g, ₹649) is a little softer and suits most skin types. Both also have aloe vera, vitamin B3 (niacinamide) and kojic acid, so over a couple of months they help skin look more even too. But comfort is the headline. More on that in is avocado night cream good.

What glutathione cream is really for

Glutathione is an antioxidant that shows up in brightening-focused skincare. In a cream, think of it as one part of a team aimed at a fresher, more radiant look. Our Glutathione Cream pairs it with vitamin C, kojic acid, niacinamide and aloe vera.

Let's be clear about one thing, because the internet isn't. Glutathione cream does not change your natural skin colour. It isn't meant to change skin tone, and anyone selling it that way is overselling. What it can do, with steady use and daily sunscreen, is help skin look brighter, less dull and more even over a few months. The glutathione cream benefits guide goes into the detail.

Texture and how each feels in Indian weather

This matters more than people expect. A cream you dislike the feel of is a cream you'll stop using by week two.

  • Chennai or Mumbai humidity: both work, in a thin layer. With either one, half a pea is often plenty, and let it settle under the fan before bed.
  • Delhi or Lucknow winter, heater on: avocado wins. Dry air pulls water from skin all night, and a richer cream holds it in.
  • AC office, AC bedroom: avocado at night for comfort. Even oily skin can feel tight after a full day under the vent.
  • Oily or pimple-prone skin: start with a very thin layer every second night, or try the gentle Avocado Glow Cream 15g (₹399) first. See avocado cream for oily skin.

Who each one suits (and who should skip)

Pick avocado cream if

Your skin feels dry, tight or rough, you're in your 30s and noticing skin isn't as plump-feeling as before, or you just want one simple night cream at a fair price. It's also the easier start if you've never used a night cream.

Pick glutathione cream if

Your skin is fairly comfortable already but looks flat, tired or uneven, especially after a summer of two-wheeler rides and sun. You're happy to wear sunscreen every morning and wait a couple of months.

Honestly, skip glutathione cream if

You're hoping it will change your skin colour. It won't, and you'll be disappointed. Also skip it for now if your skin is irritated, peeling or freshly sunburnt. Calm it first with a gentle moisturiser. If you have melasma or patches that are spreading, see a dermatologist before buying anything, including ours.

Can you use avocado cream and glutathione cream together?

Yes, and this is how a lot of people get the best of both. You don't need to layer them on top of each other the same night. Two easy ways:

  1. Alternate nights. Glutathione cream one night, avocado cream the next. Simple, and each jar lasts twice as long.
  2. Glutathione most nights, avocado when skin feels dry. Good for winter or after a long day in AC.
  3. Light morning, rich night. If you prefer, a thin layer of glutathione cream in the morning under sunscreen, and avocado cream at night. Sunscreen is not optional here.

Both of our creams contain kojic acid, so don't double up on extra brightening serums at the start. Add one new product at a time, two weeks apart, and patch test each one on the side of your neck or behind the ear for a day or two first. Our kojic acid vs glutathione guide explains how those two ingredients differ.

Price per month

Sticker price can mislead. What matters is what a month costs at a pea-sized amount each night. Based on the typical jar life in our how long does a jar of night cream last guide:

  • Avocado Night Cream, 30 g, ₹649: lasts about 6–8 weeks, so roughly ₹350–₹465 a month.
  • Avocado Korean Night Cream, 25 g, ₹649: about 5–6 weeks, roughly ₹465–₹555 a month.
  • Glutathione Cream, 30 g, ₹1,499: about 6–8 weeks, roughly ₹805–₹1,070 a month.
  • Alternating Avocado Night Cream and Glutathione Cream: both jars stretch, so roughly ₹580–₹770 a month for the pair.

These are estimates, not promises. Generous layers or using it on the neck too will shorten them.

Short answers

Is avocado cream or glutathione cream better for dry skin? Avocado cream. It's built for comfort and moisture, which is what dry skin needs first.

Does glutathione cream change your skin colour? No. It can help skin look brighter and more radiant, but it doesn't change your natural skin tone.

Can I use both on the same night? You can, in thin layers, but alternating nights is simpler and gentler, especially at the start.

Do I need sunscreen with these? Yes. Both of our creams contain kojic acid, so wear sunscreen every morning.

Which is cheaper per month? Avocado Night Cream, at roughly ₹350–₹465 a month versus roughly ₹805–₹1,070 for Glutathione Cream.

This is general skincare information, not medical advice. Patch test any new product, and see a dermatologist if you have a skin condition.
